The notation $(fg)(x)$ means  the product of the functions  $f(x)$ and $g(x).$

**Method 1**

To evaluate $(fg)(4),$ we find $f(4)$ and $g(4),$ and then multiply the results.

First, we find $f(4)$ and $g(4):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(4) & =4(4)-6=10 \\ g(4) & =5(4)-10=10\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we multiply the results:

$$
(fg)(4)=f(4)g(4)=10\cdot 10=100
$$

**Method 2**

First, we find $(fg)(x)$ by multiplying the two functions:

$$
\begin{aligned}(fg)(x) & =(4x-6)(5x-10) \\  & =20{x}^{2}-70x+60\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we evaluate $(fg)(4):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}(fg)(4) & =20(4)^{2}-70(4)+60 \\  & =320-280+60 \\  & =100\end{aligned}
$$
